title: Geometric stalks are inverse images of topos points
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $\mathcal C$ be either the small etale site $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] or the small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with sheaves and universes as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and [def-weil-size-convention]. For $U\to Y$ in $\mathcal C$ put $L(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_Y(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,U)$. For a sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ put $S(\mathcal F)=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\mathcal F(U)$, where $u\in L(U)$ and the index is the opposite category of pointed neighbourhoods: this is [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] in the etale case and [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] in the pro-etale case. Then the presheaf $p_*T$ with $(p_*T)(U)=\operatorname{Map}(L(U),T)$ and restriction by precomposition along $L(V)\to L(U)$ is a sheaf for every set $T$. There is an adjunction
$$S:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\rightleftarrows\mathbf{Set}:p_*,$$
and $S$ preserves finite limits. Thus this adjunction is a morphism of topoi $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, with inverse image $p^{-1}=S$; here a morphism of topoi means an adjunction whose left adjoint preserves finite limits.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal N$ be the category of pointed neighbourhoods, with arrows $h:(V,v)\to(U,u)$ satisfying $h\circ v=u$, and put $I=\mathcal N^{\mathrm{op}}$. The stalk diagram sends $h^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $\mathcal F(h):\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(V)$, not in the reverse direction. In the etale case $\mathcal N$ is cofiltered by [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]; the identity neighbourhood, fibre-product common refinements and equalizing refinements in its statement can all be formed within the chosen universe and replaced by isomorphic representatives of the site skeleton. In the pro-etale case [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] explicitly asserts that the opposite index category is filtered. Thus $I$ is filtered in both cases. It is small in $\mathcal V$: the site's objects form a $\mathcal V$-set, each lift set $L(U)$ and each set of pointed morphisms is a $\mathcal V$-set, and their set-indexed unions are $\mathcal V$-sets, by [def-weil-size-convention]. Explicitly, if $e:U^\circ\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ is the chosen representative isomorphism, use the lift $u^\circ=e^{-1}\circ u$. A pointed arrow $h:V\to U$ becomes $h^\circ=e_U^{-1}\circ h\circ e_V$, and $h^\circ v^\circ=e_U^{-1}hv=e_U^{-1}u=u^\circ$. Thus representatives give the required pointed objects and arrows, including equalizing arrows. The colimit in the statement is precisely the stalk of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] or [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. Write $\iota_{U,u}:\mathcal F(U)\to S(\mathcal F)$ for its coprojections. For every pointed arrow $h$ the cocone identity is $\iota_{V,v}\mathcal F(h)=\iota_{U,u}$. A sheaf map $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ induces $S(\alpha)$ by $S(\alpha)\iota^{\mathcal F}_{U,u}=\iota^{\mathcal G}_{U,u}\alpha_U$; naturality of $\alpha$ makes this a cocone, and uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives the identity and composition laws, so $S$ is a functor.

proof.text: For a covering $\{U_i\xrightarrow{f_i}U\}$ in the small etale site and a lift $u\in L(U)$, the arrows $f_i$ are etale and jointly surjective by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] to this family and to the geometric point $u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$. Its field is algebraically closed, as required by [def-weil-geometric-point]. We obtain an index $i$ and $u_i:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U_i$ with $f_i\circ u_i=u$, using the very same field $\Omega$. Hence $\coprod_i L(U_i)\to L(U)$ is surjective in the etale case.

For a covering $\{U_i\xrightarrow{f_i}U\}$ in the pro-etale site and $u\in L(U)$, the family is fpqc and all $f_i$ are weakly etale by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Base change along $u$ and set $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\times_U U_i$. The projections $Z_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ form an fpqc covering by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], so some $Z_i$ has a point $z$, by the joint-surjectivity consequence explicitly included in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Its projection is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $z$; schemes are locally affine [def-pc-scheme]. Apply the forward implication of [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-source-locality] to the affine-open covering of $Z_i$. Thus $W\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is weakly etale, equivalently $B/\Omega$ is weakly etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field], its residue field $\kappa(z)/\Omega$ is separable algebraic. Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], it is separably closed (every nonconstant separable polynomial has a root). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed] with base field $k=\Omega$, extension $M=\kappa(z)$, and target field $\Omega$ with its identity $\Omega$-algebra structure. It gives an $\Omega$-algebra map $\kappa(z)\to\Omega$. By [def-weil-residue-field], $\kappa(z)=\mathcal O_{W,z}/\mathfrak m_z$ with its induced $\Omega$-algebra structure. Compose the germ map $B=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)\to\mathcal O_{W,z}$ with the quotient and the chosen $\Omega$-algebra map to obtain $B\to\kappa(z)\to\Omega$. Applying [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives a section $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W\to Z_i$ of the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Composing with $Z_i\to U_i$ gives $u_i$; the fibre-product equation of [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $f_i\circ u_i=u$, not merely equality of underlying points. Thus $\coprod_i L(U_i)\to L(U)$ is also surjective in the pro-etale case. All these constructions are in the chosen universes. If $e:U_i^\circ\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i$ is a representative isomorphism, take $u_i^\circ=e^{-1}\circ u_i$ and $f_i^\circ=f_i\circ e$. Then $f_i^\circ u_i^\circ=f_iee^{-1}u_i=f_iu_i=u$, so the lift equation also holds for the representative.

proof.text: For a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ in the etale site, the overlaps $U_i\times_U U_j$ are scheme fibre products by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. In the pro-etale case form the scheme fibre product $Q=U_i\times_U U_j$ using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its projection to $U_j$ is weakly etale, being the base change of the covering arrow $U_i\to U$, and its composite with $U_j\to Y$ is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. Thus $Q\to Y$ is an object by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; the site has all $Y$-morphisms, so the scheme universal property is also its site universal property. This identifies the overlaps in the sheaf condition with these scheme fibre products. Two lifts $u_i\in L(U_i)$ and $u_j\in L(U_j)$ with the same image in $L(U)$ give a unique lift to $U_i\times_U U_j$, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $a_i:L(U_i)\to T$ be a matching family for the proposed presheaf $p_*T$. For $u\in L(U)$ choose a lift $u_i$ using steps 2 and 3 and put $a(u)=a_i(u_i)$. Any two choices give a lift to the overlap, where the matching condition says the two values agree. Thus $a$ is well-defined, restricts to each $a_i$, and is unique since every $u$ lifts. This is exactly the sheaf equalizer condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], proving that $p_*T$ is a sheaf. If $L(U)$ is empty, its function set is a singleton and the same argument applies. Restrictions are precomposition with $L(V)\to L(U)$; their functoriality follows from associativity of composition. A map $T\to T'$ acts by postcomposition on all these function sets, commuting with restrictions and with composition of maps of sets. Hence $p_*$ is a functor $\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$.

For a map $a:S(\mathcal F)\to T$, define $b^a_U:\mathcal F(U)\to(p_*T)(U)$ by $b^a_U(s)(u)=a(\iota_{U,u}(s))$. For $h:V\to U$ and $v\in L(V)$ the pointed arrow $(V,v)\to(U,hv)$ yields $\iota_{V,v}(\mathcal F(h)s)=\iota_{U,hv}(s)$, by the cocone identity in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Consequently $b^a_V(\mathcal F(h)s)(v)=b^a_U(s)(hv)$, precisely naturality of $b^a$ with the stated restriction maps. Thus $b^a$ is a morphism of sheaves, since sheaf morphisms are natural transformations [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 00Y8, lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf (2); explicit forward adjunction map

proof.text: Conversely, for a sheaf map $b:\mathcal F\to p_*T$, define $c_{U,u}:\mathcal F(U)\to T$ by $c_{U,u}(s)=b_U(s)(u)$. Naturality gives $c_{V,v}\mathcal F(h)=c_{U,u}$ for every pointed arrow $h:(V,v)\to(U,u)$. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] therefore gives a unique map $a^b:S(\mathcal F)\to T$ with $a^b\iota_{U,u}=c_{U,u}$. Starting with $a$, the construction $a^{b^a}$ agrees with $a$ after every $\iota_{U,u}$, so equals $a$ by uniqueness. Starting with $b$, one has $b^{a^b}_U(s)(u)=b_U(s)(u)$ for every $U,s,u$, so recovers $b$. For $\alpha:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$, the equality $S(\alpha)\iota^{\mathcal F'}_{U,u}=\iota^{\mathcal F}_{U,u}\alpha_U$ from step 1 gives $b^{a\circ S(\alpha)}=b^a\circ\alpha$. For $t:T\to T'$ the formula gives $b^{t\circ a}=(p_*t)\circ b^a$. Thus the inverse bijections are natural in both variables, proving $S\dashv p_*$.

source.place: Tag 00Y8, lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf (2); explicit inverse and naturality

proof.text:
Let $J$ be a finite category and $j\mapsto\mathcal F_j$ a diagram of sheaves of sets on $\mathcal C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], its limit $\mathcal H$ is the sheaf $\mathcal H(U)=\varprojlim_j\mathcal F_j(U)$ with the sectionwise projections. Use the same small filtered category $I$ from step 1 for every $j$. The restrictions and the diagram's natural transformations define the functor $M:I\times J\to\mathbf{Set}$ with $M((U,u),j)=\mathcal F_j(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] its canonical comparison is a bijection, yielding
$$S(\mathcal H)=\varinjlim_{(U,u)\in I}\varprojlim_{j\in J}\mathcal F_j(U)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \varprojlim_{j\in J}\varinjlim_{(U,u)\in I}\mathcal F_j(U)=\varprojlim_{j\in J}S(\mathcal F_j).$$
It is the comparison induced by the limit projections, by its stated construction from projections and coprojections. This includes the empty $J$ (the terminal object), as well as finite products and equalizers, so $S$ preserves finite limits. Together with the adjunction from steps 5 and 6, this is an adjunction with finite-limit-preserving left adjoint, hence a morphism of topoi $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ and its inverse image is the specified stalk functor $S$.
